### Observed differences

- In the later window, A19 and A20 occur much later in traces: their mean relative position rises from about 0.36 to about 0.67 for both. [POS001, POS002]
- A21 and A22 occur much earlier: their mean relative position falls from about 0.65 to about 0.38. [POS003, POS004]
- A19 and A20 are now followed by A28 in about 98% and 97% of their outgoing transitions, whereas before they were followed by A23 in about 100% and 99%. [DIR001, DIR002]
- A21 and A22 are now followed by A23 in about 50% and 46% of transitions, whereas before they were followed by A28 in about 47% and 51%. [DIR003, DIR004]
- A27 is now followed by A20 or A19 in about 98% of transitions combined, instead of A22 or A21 as before. [DIR005]
- A38 is now followed by A22 or A21 in about 93% of transitions combined, instead of A19 or A20 as before. [DIR008]
- The order between A19/A20 and A21/A22/A23/A27 reversed: before, A19/A20 preceded those activities in about half of traces; in the later window, those activities precede A19/A20 in about half of traces. [REL001–REL012]
- A21 and A22 now precede A23, whereas before A23 preceded them. [REL009, REL011, LAG001, LAG003]
- A36 became less frequent: mean occurrences per trace fell from 0.39 to 0.18, and trace participation from about 24% to 13%. [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural reordering in which A19 and A20 moved later in the process, while A21, A22, A23, and A27 moved earlier. In the later window, A19 and A20 are followed by A28 instead of A23, A21 and A22 are followed by A23 instead of A28, and A27 and A38 also shift to the new order. This is directly shown by successor changes, position shifts, and pairwise order reversals that are consistent across many activity pairs. A competing explanation based only on random sampling differences is unlikely given the size and consistency of the changes, although the exact boundaries of the reordered block cannot be fully determined from these indicators. The decrease in A36 occurrence appears as an additional, separate change.
